# Reservoir&lt;T&gt;

A reservoir sample being built.

```rux
pub struct Reservoir<T> {
    // private fields
}
```

Offer every item of the stream in turn and the reservoir ends holding a uniformly chosen subset of whatever
arrived, each subset of that size equally likely. The caller owns the storage, and its length is the sample
size.

## Type parameters

| Name | Description   |
| ---- | ------------- |
| `T`  | the item type |

## Related

<h3 id="offer"><code>Offer&lt;G, T&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Offer<G: RandomGenerator, T>(generator: &var G, reservoir: &var Reservoir<T>, item: T)
```

Offers `item` to `reservoir`.
Algorithm R: while the reservoir has room the item is kept outright, and afterwards the item replaces a
uniformly chosen existing entry with probability equal to the sample size over the number seen. That is what
keeps every subset equally likely at every moment, not merely at the end — so a stream can be cut short and
the sample is still uniform over what arrived.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Reservoir.rux#L56)
